web/execution/preflight.py:R5:bind_profi: R5 `if not isinstance(runtime_source, AWSS3Source): raise TypeError(...)`. This is the ADR-032 NOMINAL check — `isinstance` against a concrete class ELSPETH defines (`AWSS3Source`, plugins/sources/aws_s3_source.py) — over a Tier-1 value: `source` is read out of `bundle.sources` on a `PluginBundle` this process built from its own frozen plugin registry, never from an external payload. R5's stated concern (isinstance masking a contract violation) is inapplicable at this site because the negative arm RAISES: nothing is admitted, coerced, or defaulted when the check fails. What it protects: the very next statement calls `runtime_source._bind_profiled_audit_identity(identity, audit_safe_config=options)`, which attaches the operator-profiled S3 audit identity (profile alias + relative key) that the audit trail later uses to attribute the read; binding that nominal safe-evidence identity onto anything but the owned implementation would hand audit provenance to an object whose reader we do not control. `type(runtime_source) is AWSS3Source` was considered and rejected: it buys no correctness here (the negative arm raises either way) and would silently add this plugin class to the tree's undocumented CLOSED-type commitments (docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md, 2026-08-29 entry), which is a tree-wide contract change made for a lint. Invalidated if the negative arm ever stops raising, or if `bundle.sources` is ever fed plugin instances built outside the frozen registry.

R5 `if not isinstance(runtime_transform, AWSTextractDocumentAnalysis): raise TypeError(...)`. Identical shape and identical reasoning to the `bind_profiled_s3_source_audit_identities` entry above, on the transform side: `wired.plugin` comes off `bundle.transforms` of an ELSPETH-built `PluginBundle` (Tier 1), the check is the ADR-032 nominal form against a concrete owned class (`AWSTextractDocumentAnalysis`, plugins/transforms/aws/textract_document_analysis.py), and the negative arm raises `TypeError` rather than admitting anything. It guards the following `runtime_transform._bind_profiled_audit_identity(identity, audit_safe_config=options)` call, which binds the operator-profiled Textract audit identity used for audit attribution. `type(x) is ...` rejected for the same reason: it would pin a new closed-type commitment on a plugin class to clear a lint, with no behavioural gain. Invalidated if the negative arm stops raising or if `bundle.transforms` carries plugins built outside the frozen registry.

web/execution/fanout_guard.py:R6:_estima: R6 `except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, csv.Error, json.JSONDecodeError): return None`. The values being read are Tier 3 — the contents of user-supplied source files on disk, parsed as text/CSV/JSON — and the handler set is narrow and matched exactly to the IO and parse work in the `try`. `return None` is not a swallow: None is this function's declared vocabulary for "cardinality unknown", and the control that makes it safe is `record_source` in `_trace_upstream_fanout`, which is the only caller. On `estimated_rows is None` it sets `unknown_source_seen = True` and `has_unknown_cardinality = True`, clears `source_estimated_rows` to None, and appends an explicit `...estimated_rows=unknown` marker to `source_markers`; `_FanoutTrace.has_unknown_cardinality` then feeds the guard's risk decision, where an unknown-cardinality source pins the fanout risk high rather than letting the pipeline through. So an unreadable or corrupt source file makes the guard MORE conservative and is recorded in the audit markers — the opposite of a silent default, and never an invented row count. R6 misfires because `_handler_is_silent` classifies `return None` as a default return. Invalidated if the handler is widened beyond these IO/parse errors, if it starts returning a number instead of None, or if `record_source` ever stops escalating on None.
web/execution/accounting.py:R6:load_run_: R6 `except ValidationError as exc:` around the per-run `RunAccounting(...)` construction. The exception is pydantic's, raised when shape-valid counts still contradict the response model's cross-field invariants (token balance, routing subsets). The handler is an ACCUMULATOR, not a swallow — the documented healthiest validator shape in this tree (docs/agents/recent-code-hints.md, 2026-08-29 R6-on-accumulator entry): it names the failure by writing `corrupt[run_id] = RunAccountingCorruption(landscape_run_id=run_id, violations=_bounded_violations([...]))`, so the run ships an explicit corruption marker INSTEAD of accounting and no closure claim is possible for it. The controls, by symbol: (a) `RunAccountingCorruption` + `_bounded_violations` carry the per-run integrity fact into `RunAccountingBatch.corrupt`; (b) the single-run reader `load_run_accounting_from_db` re-reads that map and RAISES `ValueError` with the violations for its own caller, so the run's own completion path fails loudly rather than settling a status off missing accounting; (c) `RunAccountingBatch.accounting` never gains an entry for a corrupt run, so no consumer can read a defaulted or partial number. Per-run isolation is the point: this is a batch reader for the operator run list, and one run's contradiction must not 500 the whole batch or erase healthy runs' accounting. The pydantic messages appended are field names and counts only (`include_url=False, include_context=False, include_input=False`), so no payload text leaks into the violation strings. Invalidated if the handler ever stops writing a `corrupt` entry, if it starts constructing a partial/defaulted `RunAccounting`, or if `load_run_accounting_from_db` stops raising on a corrupt entry.
web/execution/outputs.py:R6:_is_path_in_: R6 `except OSError: return False` around `fs_path.resolve()`. The value is Tier 3 (a filesystem path recorded on an artifact row, resolved against real on-disk state) and `return False` is the RESTRICTIVE answer: an unresolvable path — symlink loop/ELOOP, broken component, FS error — is treated as NOT inside the sink allowlist, so the UI withholds the Download affordance and the `/content` endpoint refuses to serve the bytes. This is the fail-closed direction the doctrine prescribes for a security allowlist; the permissive default (`return True`) would be the vulnerability, and `return False` cannot over-authorize. It matches the function's own declared posture that `session_id=None` fails closed, and the module docstring's framing that filesystem state is allowed to be False because a purged or moved file is a fact, not an error. No audit evidence is lost: the artifact row is untouched and still enumerated in the manifest — only the download affordance is withheld. R6 misfires because `_handler_is_silent` classifies `return False` as a default return. Invalidated if the handler is changed to `return True` on OSError, or if this function's result is ever used to AUTHORIZE serving bytes rather than to WITHHOLD an affordance.
web/execution/outputs.py:R6:_classify_st: R6 `except OSError: continue` around `fs_path.resolve()` inside the `for fs_path in fs_paths` loop. The value is Tier 3 (an artifact's recorded filesystem path resolved against real on-disk state). `continue` does not end the classification: it abandons only THIS path and lets the loop test the remaining `fs_paths` against the blob / payload / outputs layouts, so a multi-path artifact is still classified from whichever of its paths resolves. When no path resolves into a known layout the loop terminates at the function's final `return "unknown"` — the explicit, documented outcome, and the conservative one: `unknown` asserts nothing about internal-storage status the function could not verify, which is exactly the direction that keeps a raw configured sink path from leaking back into the UI (elspeth-52af16f9ae, the frontend regex heuristic this discriminator replaced). Classification is deliberately independent of on-disk existence — `Path.resolve()` does not require the target to exist, so only a genuine FS error (ELOOP, permission, broken component) reaches this handler, and a merely purged blob still classifies as `blob`. Nothing is defaulted permissively and no audit record is altered. R6 misfires because `continue` is neither a raise nor a non-default return. Invalidated if the handler starts returning a concrete storage kind, or if `unknown` ever becomes a permissive/authorizing answer rather than the withholding one.
web/execution/completion_gates.py:R5:par: R5 `if not isinstance(raw, Mapping): raise ValueError(...)` on `composer_meta[COMPLETION_GATES_META_KEY]`. This is the ADR-032 parse point for a JSON-round-tripped envelope read back off our own `composition_states` row: Tier 1 by writer, but round-tripped through JSON, so shape is asserted once here and the function then constructs the owned `CompletionGateFacts` / `AdvisorSignoffGateFact` types that every downstream consumer reads. The check masks nothing — the negative arm RAISES `ValueError` naming the offending type, because a malformed present value means corruption or writer drift, and this parser feeds a completion GATE whose job is to withhold `completion_ready`. `type(raw) is dict` is not correct here: the declared parameter contract is `Mapping[str, Any]`, and an exact-type test would send every non-dict Mapping down the corruption arm on a shape the contract admits. Absence is handled separately and explicitly above by membership probes (`COMPLETION_GATES_META_KEY not in composer_meta` -> None for historical/fork-revert rows), so this check only ever sees a value the writer actually persisted. Pinned by tests/unit/web/execution/test_validation_trust_tier.py::test_completion_gate_parser_has_only_explicit_adjudication_candidates, which declares exactly these two R5s and asserts no other tier-model finding survives in this file. Invalidated if this function ever stops raising on a malformed present value, or is fed anything other than the `composer_meta` mapping of a `composition_states` record.

R5 `if not isinstance(raw_signoff, Mapping): raise ValueError(...)` on the `advisor_signoff` gate value. Same parse point, same Tier-1-persisted-but-JSON-round-tripped value, same raising negative arm as the `composer_meta.completion_gates` entry above — this is the second shape assertion in the one ADR-032 boundary, validating the nested gate envelope before its required fields are read. It is the last shape gate before `AdvisorSignoffGateFact(detail=..., for_graph=...)` is constructed; without it a non-mapping `advisor_signoff` would reach the membership-form field reads. Absence is again handled explicitly above (`_ADVISOR_SIGNOFF_GATE_KEY not in raw` -> `CompletionGateFacts(advisor_signoff=None)`, the clean-turn `{}` case), so this check only sees a value the writer persisted, and every required field below it (`status`, `detail`, `for_graph`) is read in membership form and raises on absent-or-malformed. `type(x) is dict` rejected for the same contract reason as above. Pinned by the same declaration test. Invalidated under the same conditions.
